claims.explanation: MRS-1220 is a potent and selective antagonist of the A3 adenosine receptor (ADORA3), and its antiproliferative/cytotoxic effects likely depend on A3 receptor expression and downstream signaling. The most sensitive lines are enriched for RAS/RTK-MAPK pathway activation (KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, MAP2K1, NF1 mutations) and PI3K pathway alterations (PTEN loss, PIK3CA mutation), suggesting that A3 antagonism selectively kills cells with constitutive proliferative and survival signaling. Conversely, lines with intact or alternative survival pathways, or those lacking these driver alterations, are less affected.

features.basis: MRS-1220 is a selective A3 antagonist; A3 expression is required for its effects (PMID 9364471, 10731034)

Observed enrichment of BRAF mutations in sensitive melanoma lines (IGR37, K029AX, LOXIMVI)
Observed enrichment of EGFR mutations in sensitive lung lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, KYSE270)
Observed PTEN mutations in sensitive lines (ZR751, FTC133, 786O)
Observed PIK3CA mutations in sensitive lines (HGC27, KYSE510, SNU840)
Observed NF1 mutations in sensitive lines (FTC133, BICR6, LOXIMVI)
Observed MAP2K1 mutation in sensitive line NCIH1437
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so not selective; may be weakly protective
Observed in several resistant lines (MHHES1, S117, IPC298)
Observed in resistant lines (KE39, HEC265)
Observed in resistant lines (HCC95, UO31)
